item.title: Living in Vione and working in Graubünden: a guide to the frontier
item.description: Frontier Vione-Grisioni: taxation, G permit, source tax, LAMal and insurance. Advantages, disadvantages and practical checklist for the transfer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Vione (Lombardy) to Grisons: legal cross-border route with Permit G - Withholding tax ONLY in Switzerland, no double taxation (1976 Convention) - New Agreement January 2024: €10,000 exemption for new cross-border workers, €7,500 for those before 17.7.2023
## Key facts - **What**: Residence in Vione (Brescia), work in Grisons, Permit G regime - When: New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Where: Vallecamonica borders Italian Switzerland and the canton of Grisons - Who: Cross-border workers INPS Italy, SEM (Swiss authority), Italian Revenue Agency - Tax: Withholding tax in Switzerland, tax credit in Italy form 730 (CE section) - Exemption: €10,000 annually (new), €7,500 (cross-border workers before 17.7.2023), transitional regime 2024–2033
Living in Vione and working in Grisons is a cross-border commuting choice increasingly considered by those seeking job opportunities in Switzerland while maintaining roots in the Lombard Vallecamonica. The phenomenon is not new, but with the New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024, the tax rules have been further clarified and simplified. Cross-border workers pay withholding tax exclusively in Switzerland on their employment income, avoiding double taxation mechanisms: the 9 December 1976 Italian-Swiss Convention ensures that Italy automatically recognizes the tax credit through the 730 model (CE section). Those choosing this route must also consider practical aspects beyond taxation: daily commuting, the cost of living in Switzerland, health insurance (LAMal), contributions to AVS and LPP, possible tax refunds.
### How the tax regime works The cross-border worker residing in Vione pays withholding tax in Switzerland directly from the Grisons employer. Italy recognizes this payment as a tax credit in the 730 model, avoiding double taxation. The December 2020 New Cross-Border Agreement (ratified by Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, effective from 1 January 2024) introduced the exemption: new cross-border workers (hired after 17 July 2023) benefit from €10,000 annually of income exempt from Italian taxation; those who were already cross-border workers before that date maintain €7,500 of exemption in a transitional regime that continues until 2033.
### Permit and documentation The cross-border worker working in Grisons needs Permit G, issued by the Migration Section (SEM) of the canton of Grisons. The 1976 Convention establishes that the canton of employment (Grisons) is the main place of taxation. This normative clarity eliminates jurisdictional conflicts between Italian INPS and Swiss authorities. ### Cost of living and net income A Vione-Grigioni cross-border worker faces a significant cost of living gap between Vallecamonica and Switzerland. Although the gross Swiss salary is higher than the Lombard one, expenses in Switzerland (rent, food, transportation, insurance, municipal taxes) are considerably higher. The net advantage of the Swiss income must be calculated net of: - AVS (employee contribution 5.3%) - AI/IPG (annual taxation, variable cantonal percentage) - Canton of Grisons tax - Possible LPP contributions (professional pension) A [cross-border salary calculator](nav:calculator) helps compare the gross CH with the net IT after taxes and refunds.
### Health insurance (LAMal) and pension Cross-border workers with Permit G have the **right of choice**: they can keep the Italian insurance with INPS/INAIL or choose the Swiss LAMal (Federal Health Insurance). The choice must be made before starting work and affects the entire duration of the employment relationship.
Swiss LAMal: covers care in Switzerland with adult deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 according to the chosen plan. Premiums vary by age and canton (Grigioni often competitive). Includes benefits in Switzerland and partially abroad.
Italian INPS: covers the cross-border worker in Italy and, with agreements, also in Switzerland. Contributions are managed autonomously by INPS. Less expensive if the cross-border worker qualifies for the favorable regime.
In addition to health insurance, the cross-border worker pays pension contributions: AVS (old-age, disability, survivors' pension) from the first day of work; LPP (mandatory professional pension) from the age of 25, with rates varying by age group (approximately 7–18% of the paycheck).
### Advantage and disadvantage scenarios A young cross-border worker (25–35 years), without dependents, often benefits from the gross Swiss salary and pension accumulation (AVS/LPP). The advantage decreases if: - They have dependents in Italy to support (Swiss income is proportionally lower) - They opt for LAMal with high premiums (e.g., large families) - They face significant commuting costs (gas, Swiss vignette CHF 40/year, parking, car maintenance, highways A2/A9) - They do not qualify for the €10,000 exemption (if a new cross-border worker after 17.7.2023)
### Tax refunds and declaration The Italian cross-border worker declares Swiss income to the Agenzia Entrate using the 730 or Unico form. They attach the Swiss withholding certificate (Quellensteuerbeleg), obtainable from the employer by February. The Agenzia Entrate automatically applies the tax credit for the Swiss withholding (CE section of the 730), avoiding double taxation. If the Italian + Swiss income exceeds certain thresholds, the cross-border worker may receive a refund (tax refund). Verify annually with your CAF or tax advisor.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Checklist: step by step
#### 1. Documents and permits (first month) 1. Request a residence certificate from the Municipality of Vione 2. Obtain a work contract or job offer from the Grisons employer 3. Contact the SEM office of the Grisons canton (Graubünden Landquart) or local branches for the Permit G application 4. Prepare a valid foreign identity document (passport or Italian ID card) 5. Submit the application with a copy of the contract and residence certificate
#### 2. Tax and financial aspects (first month, before starting) 1. Contact the Tax Agency (competent office for Vallecamonica/Brescia) to align the tax code and cross-border declarations 2. Choose the pension scheme BEFORE starting work: - Stay in INPS: request voluntary AGO management or INAIL integration - Switch to Swiss AVS/LPP: notify the employer, register with the competent Swiss authority 3. Evaluate the cost of LAMal (compare online at least 2-3 Swiss insurers) vs. maintaining INPS 4. Use a [cross-border paycheck calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate gross Grisons and net Italy after taxes and refunds 5. Consult the [cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living) Vione vs. destination Grisons communes (rent, food, transport, gasoline)
#### 3. Insurance (first month) 1. If you choose LAMal: contact accredited Swiss insurers (e.g., Helsana, Visana, KPT), choose a basic or intermediate plan, activate coverage starting from the first day of work 2. If you stay in INPS: notify the employer of your intention to maintain Italian INPS, integrate with INAIL if required by the type of work 3. Inform the Italian car insurance of the change of residence (circumscription reported on the green card)
#### 4. Commuting and logistics (before starting) 1. Verify the route Vione → Grisons workplace: distance, available means (car, trains, buses) 2. If you use a private car: - Purchase the Swiss vignette (CHF 40/year, mandatory for highways) - Evaluate daily gasoline costs - Roadside assistance: verify car insurance coverage in Switzerland 3. If you use public transport: - Trenord subscriptions (Lombardy, Brescia-Como-Lecco) - Swiss Railways: RhB (Rhätische Bahn) or SBB for Grisons routes - Request company subscriptions (often the employer provides or contributes)
#### 5. Annual tax declarations (January-May of the following year) 1. By February: request the withholding certificate (Quellensteuerbeleg) and pay slips from the Swiss employer 2. March-May: submit the 730 form to the Tax Agency attaching the Swiss certificate, bank statements, and any LAMal/INPS documentation 3. The Tax Agency automatically applies the tax credit (quadro CE): no further action required 4. Check for any refunds (rebates) that will be paid in the following months
### Next steps Before deciding to move, [access the calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate the monthly paycheck from Grisons and the net Italy after taxes and tax refunds. Compare the [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) between Vione and the main Grisons communes where you can find work or accommodation. Contact the permits office in the Grisons canton (tel. +41 81 xxx xxxx or official SEM email) for real processing times of the Permit G application. Finally, follow the INPS or Swiss AVS registration process: the pension choice is often irreversible, so evaluate it carefully before starting.

item.description: Berbenno-Grisioni Frontier? Guide to taxes, AVS contributions, LAMal and economic convenience of working in Switzerland and living in Italy.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement from 1 January 2024: new Italian-Swiss tax rules - Allowance of €10,000 for new cross-border workers, €7,500 for old (transitional regime until 2033) - Withholding tax deducted ONLY in Switzerland: AVS 5.3% + other contributions - Optional Swiss LAMal: annual deductible CHF 300–2,500
## Key facts - **What**: New Cross-Border Workers Agreement with allowances and simplified tax regime - When: Effective from 1 January 2024 - Who: Cross-border workers with Permit G residing in Italy and working in Switzerland - Where: Grisons (Switzerland) and Berbenno di Valtellina (Lombardy, Italy) - AVS rate: 5.3% (employee share) - Allowance for new cross-border workers: €10,000 annually on Italian income
Those living in Berbenno di Valtellina and working in Grisons fall within the intersection of two tax systems. From 1 January 2024, the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement (signed on 23 December 2020, ratified by Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023) regulates the tax treatment of those working in Switzerland and residing in Italy.
The key rule: the withholding tax on employment income is deducted only in Switzerland. Italy does not practice double withholding but applies the tax credit in the CE section of the 730 form to avoid double taxation. The Italian-Swiss Convention to avoid double taxation, signed on 9 December 1976, constitutes the normative foundation of this mechanism.
The New Agreement has introduced a crucial element: the allowance on Italian income. Cross-border workers who acquired the status after 17 July 2023 benefit from an allowance of €10,000 annually. Those who were already cross-border workers before that date enjoy an exemption of €7,500, with a transitional regime valid until 2033. This means that the Italian taxable base is reduced by this amount before the application of the tax.
### What changes in the Swiss pay slip
Swiss social contributions are deducted directly by the employer in Grisons. The cross-border worker pays: - AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance)/AI (Disability Insurance)/IPG (Income Replacement Allowance): 5.3% (employee share) - AD (Unemployment Insurance)/AC: 1.1% annually up to CHF 148,200 - LAINF (Accident Insurance): 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector - LPP (Occupational Pension Scheme, 2nd pillar): 7–18% based on age (from the 25th year)
In Italy, IRPEF is applied in brackets: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. However, the allowance of €10,000 (or €7,500 for old cross-border workers) significantly reduces the Italian taxable base.
### Swiss health insurance and the available option
The [LAMal (Swiss health insurance)](nav:health) represents a relevant decision. Cross-border workers with Permit G have the right to choose: they can remain in the Italian health system or join a Swiss health insurance fund. If they choose LAMal, the annual deductible varies from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 depending on the chosen level of coverage. Those who remain in the Italian system contribute through the national mandatory regime without additional cross-border costs. If you have decided to move to Berbenno and work in the Grisons, the economic convenience assessment requires looking beyond the gross salary. The tax structure and double taxation mechanisms offer concrete advantages for those who know how to read them. A typical scenario: a cross-border worker with an annual gross Swiss income is subject to withholding in Switzerland (AVS 5.3% + contributions for about 8–10% of the gross). Then they declare the income in Italy, where they benefit from a €10,000 exemption that reduces the taxable base. If the gross income is modest, it might not even exceed the highest IRPEF brackets, generating a favorable overall tax burden compared to a traditional Italian worker. ### Cost of Living and Geographical Advantages of Valtellina Berbenno di Valtellina is located in the province of Sondrio, in Valtellina. The area generally has a lower cost of living compared to the larger urban agglomerations in Ticino, with lower real estate prices and rents. At the same time, the geographical proximity to the Grisons and the border crossings (such as Brogeda) represents a logistical advantage: commuting times remain manageable for those working in Switzerland. A cross-border worker residing in Berbenno maintains access to Italian services and communities—school, local healthcare, commerce—while working and contributing to a Swiss pension system (AVS/LPP). In the long term, this hybrid can be advantageous: the Swiss AVS pension is generally higher than the Italian pension for equivalent contribution amounts. ### Crucial Decisions: Employer and Insurance The choice of canton and company in the Grisons influences the contribution burden and social services. Some employers in the Grisons offer generous private LPP coverage, which increases the cross-border worker's pension savings beyond the legal minimum. The choice of health insurance (Swiss LAMal versus the Italian system) depends on the health profile and family needs. Those who opt for LAMal must evaluate the chosen deductible and the annual premium; those who remain in the Italian system do not incur additional cross-border costs beyond national contributions.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). If the decision to move to Berbenno and work in Graubünden is final, the administrative procedure includes some crucial steps. Each phase has its own deadlines and precise tax consequences that no cross-border worker should underestimate.

## In brief - New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Withholding tax deducted ONLY in Switzerland - Permit G requires non-residence in Switzerland - Social protection: Swiss AVS, LPP, LAMal
## Key facts - **What**: Cross-border work Italy-Switzerland - When: New Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Where: Como-Grigioni border crossings - Who: Cross-border workers residing in Italy - Permit: Permit G (cross-border)
If you decide to move to Mese to work in the Swiss canton of Grisons, your tax situation changes significantly compared to living in Ticino. The New Cross-Border Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and effective from 1 January 2024, represents the main regulatory framework for cross-border workers operating between Italy and Switzerland.
### Permit G and residence
To work in Grisons as a cross-border worker, you need Permit G, which does not allow you to live permanently in Switzerland. This means your residence remains in Mese, Italy, while your work is in Switzerland. item.title: Church-Grison Frontiers: Tax Guide and Practice
item.description: Living in Chiesa in Valmalenco and working in Graubünden: new 2024 agreement, exemptions €7,500-€10,000, Swiss taxation and Italian tax credit.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New cross-border agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Exemption €7,500 (old cross-border workers) or €10,000 (new) - Withholding tax deducted ONLY in Switzerland - Italian tax credit cancels double taxation
## Key facts - **What**: New Italy-Switzerland Cross-Border Agreement - When: Signed 23 December 2020, effective 1 January 2024 - Ratification: Law 83/2023 (Italy, 13 June 2023) - Regime: Transitional 2024-2033 for old cross-border workers - Exemption old: €7,500 annually - Exemption new: €10,000 annually - Convention: Italy-Switzerland, 9 December 1976
A cross-border worker residing in Chiesa in Valmalenco who works in Graubünden is now in a regulatory scenario transformed by the New Cross-Border Agreement that came into force on 1 January 2024. This pact, signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, completely redesigns the tax rules on employment income for those who reside in Italy and work in Switzerland.
### The structure of exemptions in the New Agreement
The agreement introduces a graduated system of exemptions according to the status of the cross-border worker. Those who were already holders of a G Permit before 17 July 2023 benefit from an annual exemption of €7,500 from Italian taxable income. Those who acquire cross-border status from 2024 onwards enjoy a more generous exemption, equal to €10,000 annually. This differential reflects a desire to encourage new rights while protecting consolidated positions through a ten-year transitional regime (2024-2033). After 2033, exemptions may be subject to changes in subsequent negotiations between the two countries, with notice to the affected cross-border workers.
### How the Swiss withholding tax works
The crucial element of cross-border taxation: the withholding tax is deducted exclusively by Switzerland, not by Italy. On the gross salary, the Swiss employer automatically applies mandatory contributions: AVS/AI/IPG equal to 5.3% (employee share), unemployment contributions (AD) and competitiveness (AC) of 1.1%, accident insurance (LAINF) between 0.7 and 1.5%, and payments to the LPP pension fund which vary from 7 to 18% depending on the age bracket (from the 25th year onwards). On this basis, the Swiss federal tax is calculated and withheld, already personalized based on the data communicated at the time of hiring with the cantonal authorities. ### The Italy-Switzerland Convention and the Tax Credit
The Convention to avoid double taxation between Italy and Switzerland, signed on December 9, 1976, represents the pillar that protects the cross-border worker from being taxed completely twice on the same income. In Italy, the foreign income earned in Switzerland is subject to the personal income tax (IRPEF) with progressive rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000. However, thanks to the Convention, the Italian tax authorities recognize a tax credit equivalent to the taxes already paid in Switzerland. In the model 730 or in the income tax return, the CE section includes the amount of the Swiss withholding tax, and the Revenue Agency deducts it from the overall Italian tax liability.
### The Mechanism of the Tax Credit and Its Limits
A relevant aspect: the tax credit operates with the principle of "limited credit." If the tax paid in Switzerland (for a given income) exceeds the Italian tax that would have been due on that same amount, the credit is capped at the Italian amount. The difference in favor of Switzerland is not refunded: the cross-border worker "loses" it in terms of progressivity. Conversely, if the Swiss tax is lower, the credit is full and the cross-border worker adds the Italian completion without further charges. The final result therefore depends on the actual comparison between Swiss rates and Italian IRPEF rates on the same amount.
### Practical Advantages of the Exemption from the New Agreement 2024
With the entry into force of the New Agreement, the situation has significantly improved for cross-border workers. The exemption from the Italian taxable income represents a real discount on payments to the Italian tax authorities. An old cross-border worker who earns, for example, €50,000 gross annually in Switzerland, under the old regime would have declared the entire amount in Italy with the corresponding IRPEF taxation. With the exemption of €7,500, he declares only €42,500, reducing the Italian tax burden by about €1,700-€1,800 depending on the actual progressivity. New cross-border workers enjoy an even greater discount (€10,000), which would reduce the taxable amount to the same parameters at €40,000, with significant savings.
### The Transitional Regime and What Happens After 2033
The regime provided by the New Agreement for old cross-border workers is transitional and expires at the end of 2033. Until that date, holders of Permit G acquired before July 17, 2023, maintain the exemptions of €7,500 annually without changes. From 2034 onwards, the amount could undergo variations (upward revisions, downward revisions, or reconfirmation) according to the negotiations between Italy and Switzerland. For new cross-border workers acquired from 2024, it is not yet clearly documented what will happen after 2033; it is likely that it will continue with the same exemptions of €10,000, but it will remain subject to bilateral renegotiation.
### Swiss Pension Contributions and Pension Accumulation
The Swiss pension protection system is robust and mandatory for all employees. The first pillar (AVS — Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) is the basic public system, financed with contributions equal to 5.3% of gross salary (employee's share). The second pillar (LPP — occupational pension fund) is legally required and varies in percentage according to the worker's age, from a minimum of 7% for the youngest (from 25 years) to 18% for the age groups close to retirement. This means that the cross-border worker in Grisons accumulates Swiss pension rights progressively, with an "individual account" that grows every year in the insurer's database. At the time of retirement, he will be entitled to both the AVS pension and the LPP benefit based on the total contributions made. # ## Practical procedure: how to start as a Church-Grison border crossing Step 1: Obtaining the G Permit The regulatory prerequisite is the G Permit (border crossing permit), which authorises daily commuting between Italy and the Canton of Graubünden. The request is usually initiated by the Swiss employer with the Grison cantonal authorities or the competent body of the canton where you found work. You need a regular employment contract, proof of domicile in Italy (in Chiesa in Valmalenco) and a declaration of intent to commute. Permit G is generally valid for 5 years, renewable with simple presentation of updated documentation. Step 2: Registration with the Federal Tax Administration Once hired, the Swiss employer communicates your personal data, the Italian domicile and the structure of the paycheck to the AFC (Federal Tax Administration), which administers the tax at source at the Swiss federal level. The AFC processes the data and determines the custom source tax rate based on estimated income and the canton where you work. From this moment on, each salary is automatically withheld according to the calculated rate. Step 3: Annual tax return in Italy Each tax year, by the end of May, you must complete the Italian tax return. If you are a resident of Chiesa in Valmalenco, you will use form 730 (if you are a pure employee) You will avoid surprises in the next statement and maximize the application of available exemptions and credits. # ## Practical tools to simulate your situation Use the [calcolatore di stipendio](nav:calculator) to simulate the net paycheck in Switzerland and the overall Italian tax burden. Enter the annual gross salary in CHF, select the canton of Graubünden (which determines the federal cantonal rate), specify your age group (for the correct calculation of the LPP), indicate the marital status and the number of children. The tool will show you the estimated monthly net, total tax burden and impact of the New Deal exemption. If you are considering moving to Switzerland in the future instead of staying in the Church, the [comparatore Permesso G vs B](nav:permit-compare) helps you weigh the pros and cons of the two scenarios (border vs. Swiss resident) in terms of tax, social security and quality of life. When filling out the Italian declaration, consult an online tool for the [modello 730](nav:tax-return) or contact your Caf directly to verify the correct application of the 1976 Convention tax credit and the exemption provided by the New Frontier Agreement.

item.description: Living in San Giacomo Filippo and working in the Graubünden: G permit, €10,000 deductible, Swiss AVS/LPP, LAMal and declaration 730. Rules 2024.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement from 1 January 2024: €10,000 allowance for new cross-border workers - Withholding tax only in Switzerland; Italian tax credit via 730 - Permit G mandatory, requested through the Swiss employer
## Key facts - **What**: New Italy-Switzerland Cross-Border Workers Agreement - When: Effective 1 January 2024 (signed 23 December 2020) - Where: Cross-border workers Italy-Grisons (Grisons Canton, Switzerland) - Who: Cross-border workers category G; INPS and Swiss administration (AFC/ESTV) - Amount: €10,000 allowance for new cross-border workers, €7,500 for old (2024–2033)
Those living in San Giacomo Filippo, in the province of Sondrio (Lombardy), and working in the Swiss Grisons are in a unique position: cross-border workers subject to both Italian and Swiss regulations. On 1 January 2024, a new decisive regulation came into force—the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023—which reconfigured the tax and contribution system.
The most relevant rule is the €10,000 annual allowance for new cross-border workers. Up to this amount of Swiss employment income, Italy suspends IRPEF taxation. Above this threshold, the progressive national Italian rate applies: 23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, 43% above €50,000. Meanwhile, Switzerland withholds a withholding tax directly from the paycheck. How to avoid double taxation? The Convention against double taxation signed on 9 December 1976 between Italy and Switzerland establishes that the Swiss withholding tax is final on employment income and that Italy grants a tax credit (CE section of the 730 model) equivalent to the Swiss taxation paid. The cross-border worker files the 730 declaration, attaches the Swiss tax certificate, and recovers the difference if the Italian rate is lower.
### Permit G: the legal foundation
No cross-border worker can work in Switzerland without Permit G. It is not a concession: it is the legal authorization to stay for work purposes. The request is not submitted directly to the Swiss authorities, but through the Swiss employer. It is the company that sends the application to the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration), coordinating with the Grisons cantonal administration. The minimum documentation includes: signed employment contract, Italian residence certificate (to be requested from the Municipality), declaration of non-employment in Italy, valid passport or identity card, and specific cantonal forms. Response times vary between 4 and 12 weeks depending on the completeness of the file.
### Italian residence and annual coordination
Although you work in Switzerland, the registered residence must remain in an Italian municipality (San Giacomo Filippo or another area of Sondrio). Switzerland, not being a member of the EU or EEA, requires that Permit G be linked to a permanent foreign residence. Annually, you must renew the residence certificate with your Municipality—a simple procedure, with minimal costs and 1–2 day times. The Italian tax administration, through coordination with INPS, monitors your cross-border worker status: it is not complicated if managed regularly. ### AVS, LPP, LAINF: the Swiss pension system
Those who work in Graubünden pay Swiss social security contributions, not Italian ones. You do not pay INPS: contributions go to AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) and AI (Disability Insurance). The AVS/AI/IPG deduction amounts to 5.3% of the gross salary for the employee, with an equivalent share from the employer. This is supplemented by the accident insurance premium (LAINF) of 0.7%–1.5% at the employer's expense. Critically, contribution to the second pillar (LPP), the Swiss pension fund, is mandatory: for those aged 25 or older, the percentage varies from 7% to 18% depending on age and fund, with a split between employee and employer.
The Italian INPS remains at zero: the cross-border worker does not pay any contributions to the Italian public pension system. The future pension will be calculated entirely on the basis of AVS, with the possibility of reunification only if contributions were made to the Italian system before acquiring cross-border status. The Swiss system is structurally more generous in terms of rates relative to income, although the AVS pension is not automatically supplemented by a third Italian pillar.
### LAMal and health insurance option
For health insurance, the cross-border worker has the **right to choose**: they can enroll in LAMal (Swiss Health Insurance Act) with adult deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500, or maintain enrollment in the Italian National Health Service through INPS. Most cross-border workers opt for LAMal for its cost-effectiveness and more comprehensive coverage in Switzerland. The choice affects Italian health taxation and the overall pension strategy.
### Hypothetical scenario: paycheck calculation
Consider a cross-border worker with an employment contract and a monthly gross salary of CHF 4,500: Swiss withholdings include AVS/AI/IPG (CHF 238.50, equivalent to 5.3%), LAINF (CHF 22.50–67.50), LPP (CHF 315–810 depending on age), plus cantonal withholding tax (variable according to personal and family deductions). The Swiss net typically results in 60% to 70% of the gross, a percentage higher than the Italian average (55–60% on an equivalent RAL in EUR), thanks to the efficiency of the Swiss pension systems and lower marginal taxation on low-to-medium incomes.
### Specific tax details of the Canton of Graubünden
The Canton of Graubünden sets its own cantonal withholding tax rate. There is no 'national Swiss withholding tax': it is the canton (sometimes the municipality) that determines the rate. Graubünden is competitive compared to other cantons (not among the most expensive, but neither among the lowest). A cross-border worker residing in Lombardy and working in Graubünden pays withholding tax according to local Graubünden tables. This directly influences the tax credit claimable in Italy: higher Swiss tax equals higher Italian credit.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### How to become a cross-border worker San Giacomo Filippo–Grigioni: step-by-step procedure
Step 1: sign a Swiss employment contract. This is the absolute prerequisite. Job search can be done through Swiss job boards (Indeed.ch, LinkedIn.ch), employment agencies, or direct contacts. Without a signed concrete offer, the G Permit application does not proceed.
Step 2: the Swiss employer submits the G Permit application. You do not fill it out directly. The company sends the file to the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) of the Canton of Grisons, through the competent regional office. Response times: 4–12 weeks. Longer periods are possible if documentation is missing.
**Step 3: gather Italian documentation.** While the employer coordinates with the Swiss authorities, you prepare: residence certificate from your municipality of Sondrio (updated), declaration of non-employment in Italy (to be requested from the Chamber of Commerce or provincial labor directorate), criminal record and physical fitness if required, certified copy of identity card or passport.
Step 4: open a Swiss bank account. Not always mandatory from day 1, but most employers require it for salary payment. Banks in Grisons such as Raiffeisen Grisons or Banca Cantonale Grisons offer services to cross-border workers. Swiss IBAN necessary for Italian administrative coordination.
Step 5: register with INPS as a cross-border worker. After receiving the G Permit, do not delay: contact INPS (Sondrio branch or nearest) and communicate your status as a cross-border worker. INPS will register the file and coordinate with the Swiss AVS to avoid double administrative registrations.
### Annual 730 declaration and tax refunds
Every year, by May 31, you submit the 730 model through your trusted accountant or CAF. The 730 must include: Swiss employment income (converted to EUR at the average monthly exchange rate of the year), Swiss withholding tax paid (declared by the employer in the official certificate), claim of tax credit (CE section). If the €10,000 threshold covers your entire income, the 730 will show zero Italian tax due. If you exceed it, you pay progressive IRPEF on the excess. The difference between Swiss tax and calculated Italian IRPEF is the refund: if Switzerland has withheld more than Italy, you receive a refund; if Italy asks for more than Switzerland, you settle the difference.
### Essential document checklist
- ✓ Signed Swiss employment contract - ✓ Italian residence certificate (updated annually) - ✓ Declaration of non-employment in Italy - ✓ Criminal record and physical fitness (if required) - ✓ Valid identity card or passport copy - ✓ Annual Swiss tax certificate (for 730) - ✓ Swiss bank account IBAN - ✓ Specific SEM forms for Grisons
### Crucial deadlines and renewals
The G Permit has limited validity (usually 1–5 years). Before expiration, the employer must submit a renewal request. Failure to renew = loss of legal residence status for work. The residence certificate must be renewed annually at the municipality. The 730 declaration is mandatory by May 31 of the year following the income to be declared.
To deepen the calculation of your paycheck and estimate the net monthly amount based on your actual gross, consult the [cross-border salary calculator](nav:calculator): a reliable tool that considers the cantonal withholding tax, AVS/AI/LPP contributions, and your personal circumstances.

item.title: Living in Grosotto and working in Graubünden as a border worker
item.description: Tax exemption, commuting, cost of living: practical guide to moving to Grosotto to work in Graubünden.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - New Cross-Border Agreement from 1 January 2024: €10,000 allowance for new cross-border workers - Withholding tax deducted in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy with CE section of the 730 form - Advantages: lower cost of living, Swiss salary; disadvantages: daily mountain commuting
## Key facts - **What**: Moving to Grosotto to work in Switzerland (Grisons) - When: From 1 January 2024 (New Agreement) - Where: Grosotto (Sondrio) ↔ Grisons (Switzerland) - Who: Category G cross-border workers (employees) - Allowance: €10,000 for new cross-border workers
Grosotto is a municipality in the province of Sondrio, in northern Lombardy, Italy, strategically located near the Swiss Grisons. For the cross-border worker employed in Switzerland, moving to Grosotto represents a concrete economic alternative: the Italian cost of living is significantly lower than the Swiss cost, allowing a substantial portion of the Swiss salary to be saved.
### Tax regime from 1 January 2024
The tax regime for category G cross-border workers (employees) has been redefined by the New Cross-Border Agreement, which came into effect on 1 January 2024. New cross-border workers benefit from a €10,000 allowance on employment income. The withholding tax is deducted solely in Switzerland; in Italy, the cross-border worker declares the income in the CE section of the 730 form and uses the tax credit to avoid double taxation. Discover how to optimize your [refund rights](nav:ristorni) with the new regime. This structure, regulated by the Italian-Swiss Convention of 9 December 1976, ensures protection from double taxation.
### Moving as a conscious economic choice
Many cross-border workers already come from the Ticino-Sondrio border area. Moving to Grosotto represents a choice of continuity: staying in Italy but closer to the Grisons, maintaining the economic advantage of the local cost of living and the Swiss income in CHF. For others, it is a pure savings strategy: the cost of a home in Grosotto is significantly lower than that of comparable Swiss or Ticino municipalities. However, daily commuting involves fixed costs (fuel, maintenance, vehicle wear) that must be realistically calculated in the overall economic budget. ### Travel times and road conditions to the Grisons
The travel time from the Grosotto area to the border crossings towards the Grisons depends on the specific destination in Switzerland and the mountain road conditions. Generally, they range from less than an hour to slightly more, depending on the Grisons area where you work (Poschiavo, Tirano, Davos, Valposchiava municipalities). The main routes involve crossing Italian territory northward towards the municipalities bordering the Grisons. During the winter months, mountain roads can be affected by snow, ice, and bad weather, leading to delays and increased road safety risks. It is essential to evaluate your specific workplace in Switzerland and verify the actual travel times before making a final decision to move.
### Concrete advantages of moving
Moving to Grosotto offers tangible economic advantages. The cost of living is lower (rent, groceries, utilities, services) compared to Ticino and Switzerland, allowing for significant savings on the Swiss salary expressed in CHF. The frontier regulatory framework is established and protected by the New 2024 Agreement, which simplifies taxation and guarantees a €10,000 exemption for new cross-border workers. Additionally, access to Italian schools, healthcare, and public services is significantly cheaper than in Switzerland. The geographical location of Grosotto allows for a balance between proximity to the Swiss workplace and the economic benefits of Italian residence.
### Disadvantages and hidden costs of commuting
Daily commuting along the border involves concrete disadvantages that reduce the actual economic advantage. The costs of car maintenance (fuel, maintenance, insurance, possible tolls) are significant and reduce the savings margin. The variability of the CHF/EUR exchange rate exposes the cross-border worker to currency fluctuations, directly impacting the purchasing power of savings. The cross-border worker must manage a double administrative residence (Italy and Switzerland with Permit G), creating bureaucratic and tax complications. Finally, daily travel involves physical wear and tear, stress related to seasonal mountain weather conditions (especially in winter), and time costs (travel time) that are often underestimated in the initial assessment.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Checklist: how to prepare for the move
1. Research housing and initial financial assessment. Consult real estate portals for housing in Grosotto. Evaluate the monthly rental cost or purchase price, compare it realistically with your current situation, and estimate the actual monthly savings (net of commuting and fixed costs). Remember that moving expenses (real estate agencies, notary, moving) should be amortized over a realistic multi-year plan.
2. Verify permits and administrative notifications. Notify the Italian authorities (Grosotto municipality) of the change of residence according to standard procedures. Check with the Swiss State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) if the change of residence to Grosotto requires an official notification of your current Permit G. Keep a copy of the permit documentation and the change of address notification.
**3. Specialized tax consultation (PRIORITY).** Consult a tax expert specializing in cross-border workers before making the move. They will guide you on: registration as a resident with the Grosotto municipality, correct completion of the CE section of the 730 form with cross-border tax credit, application of the €10,000 exemption (new cross-border workers) on the 2025 declaration, verification of the Italy-Switzerland Convention of December 9, 1976 for double taxation protection.
4. Health insurance (LAMal) and health options. As a cross-border worker with Permit G, you retain the right to choose between Swiss health insurance (LAMal) and potentially supplementing with the Italian public health system. Check the annual deadlines for choosing/confirming LAMal and the franchise options (CHF 300-2500 for adults). If you previously had LAMal, contact your health insurance company to update your resident address to Grosotto.
5. Realistic calculation of car and commuting costs. Concretely evaluate the total cost of the commuting car: monthly fuel, annual maintenance, insurance, and possibly the Swiss vignette if your canton of work requires it. Calculate the cost per km and per month, and rigorously subtract this value from your net Swiss income. Also include physical wear and tear and time cost (hours lost to travel, stress, fatigue) in the final assessment of convenience.
### Tools for an informed decision
Use the [Swiss net calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate the impact of the €10,000 exemption on your paycheck after withholding taxes. Update your demographic data (Grosotto residence) and compare the resulting net with the estimated costs of the move and commuting. Consult the [cost of living comparator](nav:cost-of-living) to evaluate the economic differential between Grosotto and your previous residence (Ticino, Switzerland, other border areas).
The decision to move to Grosotto to work in Graubünden is personal and depends on economic, family, and professional factors. With careful preparation, specialized consultation, and a realistic assessment of costs, the move can represent a concrete opportunity for economic optimization for the cross-border worker.

item.title: Living in Vergiate, working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: The new 2024 Frontier Agreement makes it convenient to live in Vergiate: exemption €10,000, G permit, journey time 45-60 minutes. Taxation, AVS/LPP, LAMal and procedures.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-Border Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Exemption of €10,000 for new cross-border workers from taxable income - Vergiate-Lugano connection: 45-60 minutes via Gaggiolo border crossing - Withholding tax levied exclusively in Switzerland
## Key facts - **What**: Favourable tax regime for cross-border workers Ticino-Italy - When: From 1 January 2024 - Where: Gaggiolo border crossing (10 min), Ponte Tresa (40 km), Chiasso (50 km) - Who: Cross-border workers category G and B between Italy and Ticino - Exemption: €10,000 (new cross-border workers from 2024) - Previous regime: €7,500 for those who were cross-border workers before 17 July 2023 - Taxation: Switzerland (withheld at source); Italy avoids double taxation - Pension: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% employee, LPP 7-18% by age bracket
The new Cross-Border Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and effective from 1 January 2024, revolutionizes the tax regime for those residing in Italy and working in the Canton of Ticino. Vergiate, a municipality in the province of Varese in Lombardy, has become an ideal base for cross-border workers: quick access to major Swiss border crossings, lower cost of living compared to Lugano and Mendrisio, and a well-established road network. The €10,000 exemption significantly reduces the gross taxable income in Switzerland, benefiting especially average salaries.
The withholding tax remains levied exclusively in Switzerland, while Italy applies a tax credit on the 730 declaration (CE section) to avoid cumulative taxation. Cross-border workers who were already such before 17 July 2023 benefit from a higher exemption (€7,500) with a transitional regime until 2033. The Convention against Double Taxation between Italy and Switzerland, signed on 9 December 1976, is the regulatory framework that ensures protection from double taxation.
### Geographical location and connections to border crossings
Vergiate is located northeast of Varese, a few kilometers from the Swiss border. The nearest border crossing is Gaggiolo (Vergiate-Maroggia), reachable in 10-15 minutes by car. From here, the journey to Lugano takes about 45-60 minutes, depending on traffic conditions and the season. The alternative is the Ponte Tresa border crossing (via Sesto Calende), about 40 km and less congested during peak hours. The Chiasso border crossing, the busiest in Switzerland, is 50 km away and is useful for those working in the Sottoceneri (Mendrisio, Stabio) or in Bellinzona.
The geographical location of Vergiate significantly reduces daily commuting times compared to other municipalities in Varese. The state road 394 and the local network connect directly to the border crossings. For those who prefer public transport, AutoPostale and regional Tilo trains offer options, although less frequent during peak hours compared to private commuting. ### Swiss taxation and social security for cross-border workers
Swiss taxation for cross-border workers depends on the permit category and the applicable exemption. With the new €10,000 exemption introduced by the 2024 Agreement, a gross salary is reduced by this amount before the cantonal rate is applied. Withholding tax is deducted exclusively in Switzerland; Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit on the 730 declaration (CE section).
The mandatory Swiss contributions deducted from the paycheck include: AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance), AI (Disability Insurance), and IPG (Insurance for Loss of Earnings): 5.3% of the gross salary. These contributions fund basic retirement and disability protection. Unemployment Insurance (AI) and Credit Insurance (AC) require an additional 1.1% (with a maximum of CHF 148,200 gross income). Occupational Pension (LPP) involves a contribution between 7% and 18% of the salary, depending on the age bracket. A cross-border worker starts paying LPP from the age of 25; until that threshold, they pay only AVS/AI/IPG and AD/AC.
The Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland, signed on December 9, 1976, is the normative pillar that protects the cross-border worker from cumulative taxation. Italy applies the tax credit system: if the cross-border worker has paid taxes in Switzerland higher than those due based on the Italian IRPEF (23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001-50,000, 43% over €50,000), the difference can be recovered in the tax declaration.
### Cost of living: the economic advantage of Vergiate
Living in Vergiate, while working in Ticino, allows for significant savings. Residential rents are considerably lower than those in Lugano or Mendrisio. Basic groceries, local car taxes, and public utility services are cheaper. The economic advantage compensates, at least in part, for the daily commuting costs to the border crossings.
The choice of health insurance is crucial. Category G cross-border workers have the option: they can remain in the Swiss LAMal (with annual deductibles of CHF 300-2500 for adults) or integrate into the Italian SSN. LAMal requires complete coverage but demands regular payment of premiums; the Italian SSN is funded by work contributions but offers fewer coverage choices and longer waiting times.
The main advantage of Italian residence is economic: rents and home management costs are lower. The tax framework has been improved by the 2024 Agreement, with the €10,000 exemption reducing the gross taxable income in Switzerland. Italy DOES NOT apply additional taxes on Swiss work income, thanks to the 1976 Convention. Disadvantages include daily commuting times, vehicle wear (fuel, maintenance, insurance), the need to coordinate pension contributions between two countries, and a smaller cross-border community in Vergiate compared to communes like Mendrisio or Chiasso.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Procedure to obtain the G permit category
The G permit (cross-border) is the document required to work permanently in Ticino as an Italian resident. The application can be submitted to the Migration Section (SEM) of the canton of work or to the Police Headquarters of the province of Varese, depending on local procedures.
Generally required documents: Valid passport or identity card; Residence certificate from the Italian municipality (Vergiate or other); Employment contract or job offer from a Ticino company; Chamber of Commerce registration certificate (if self-employed); Bank statement for the last 3 months (if required). The application is processed in 4-8 weeks. Once approved, the G permit is issued for 5 years, renewable. Some cantons in Ticino require a preliminary medical examination; check with the competent cantonal office.
### Annual deadlines and mandatory obligations
Each calendar year, the cross-border worker must comply with specific deadlines. By January-February: Communicate the new Italian address to the employer and verify that withholding taxes are correct (exemption €10,000 and AVS/LPP contributions). By June 30: Submit the 730 form to the Italian Revenue Agency to recover tax credits (CE section), if Swiss withholdings exceed the Italian IRPEF due. By the end of the year: Verify that the employer has correctly paid AVS/AI contributions in Switzerland and that the LPP is active (from the 25th year of age). Upon request: Renew registration with the Ticino social security offices, if the canton requires it.
### Checklist for the transfer
Documentation and residence: (1) Gather passport, previous employment certificates, new employment contract; (2) Register with the Registry Office of the Italian municipality (Vergiate) within 8 days of arrival; (3) Obtain a residence certificate from the municipality. Permit and work: (4) Submit the G permit application to the cantonal SEM or Italian Police Headquarters; (5) Communicate the new address to the employer and request the adjustment of the pay slip (exemption €10,000, correct AVS/LPP/AD/AC contributions); (6) Verify that the employer applies the rates of the 2024 Agreement. Insurance and finance: (7) Choose between Swiss LAMal (deductible CHF 300-2500) or Italian SSN; sign the contract; (8) Open an Italian bank account to receive the salary; (9) Verify Italian car insurance and update the address with the company. Taxes and social security: (10) Register with the Italian Revenue Agency as a cross-border worker; (11) Plan the 730 declaration for the following year (by May); (12) Verify AVS/LPP registration with the Swiss employer.
A new cross-border worker can request support from Ticino trade unions (VPOD, USS, OCST) or cross-border associations, which offer advice on procedures, taxation, and social security. Use our [tax calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate your net pay slip once settled in Vergiate. Consult the [guides on permits and documents](nav:permits) for detailed clarifications on the G category procedure and processing times.

item.title: Crodo: guide for border workers working in Ticino
item.description: Crodo offers low cost of living and quick access to Ticino passes. Complete guide: G permit, tax with new 2024 agreement, AVS/LPP, LAMal, refreshments and practical procedures.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - As of January 1, 2024, the new tax agreement is in effect: old cross-border workers are exempt €7,500/year, new ones €10,000 in allowance - Crodo (VB, Piedmont) offers a lower cost of living than Ticino but maintains quick access to border crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo) - Withholding tax is paid only in Switzerland; Italy grants tax credit via the CE section of the 730 form - LAMal in G regime: choice between Swiss insurance (CHF 300–2,500 deductible) or Italian INPS
## Key facts - **What**: Living in Crodo (Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, Piedmont) and working in Canton Ticino with a G permit - When: New agreement effective from January 1, 2024 - Where: Crodo ↔ Brogeda/Gaggiolo/Chiasso border crossings towards Ticino centers (Lugano, Mendrisio, Bellinzona) - Who: Cross-border workers with a G permit and interested in moving residence - Amount: Exemption €7,500 (old cross-border workers) or allowance €10,000 (new), transitional regime 2024–2033
Crodo is becoming an increasingly popular choice among workers who want to obtain a [G permit to work in Ticino](nav:permits) while maintaining a residence in Piedmont. The town, located in the province of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, offers a concrete balance between lower housing costs compared to Canton Ticino and geographical proximity that reduces commuting times to the main Ticino work centers (Lugano, Mendrisio, Chiasso, Bellinzona, Locarno).
The entry into force of the new Switzerland-Italy tax agreement on January 1, 2024 (signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023) has introduced significant measures for cross-border workers. Cross-border workers already registered before July 17, 2023, enjoy a tax exemption of €7,500 annually in a transitional regime until 2033, while new cross-border workers benefit from an allowance of €10,000. These thresholds represent a structural incentive for those considering moving to Crodo from other Italian centers.
### Geographical position and connections to Ticino Crodo is strategically located with respect to the main border crossings to Canton Ticino. The border can be reached via Gaggiolo (state road), Brogeda, or further south through connections to Chiasso and Mendrisio. Compared to more inland Piedmont settlements (Turin, Novara, Vercelli), Crodo offers significantly shorter travel times to the offices and construction sites of Lugano, Mendrisio, and the Luganese. For cross-border workers who work in companies based in Bellinzona or Locarno, commuting remains manageable: the A2 and A9 highways, although subject to traffic variability during peak hours, ensure regular connectivity. ### Taxation: withholding tax, double taxation and refunds
For a cross-border worker living in Crodo and working in Ticino, the withholding tax is exclusively deducted in Switzerland on the pay slip. There is no immediate double taxation: Italy does not levy further on the gross amount but allows a tax credit through the CE section of the tax return (model 730 or model Unico). This mechanism is governed by the Italo-Swiss Convention on Double Taxation signed on December 9, 1976, which ensures stable legal protection.
The withholding tax rate applied by Switzerland varies according to the canton and individual incomes: in Ticino, the combined federal and cantonal rates are administered by the Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV). The tax return in Italy allows for the recovery of excess taxation if the Swiss rate is higher than the Italian one (IRPEF: 23% up to €28,000, 35% from €28,001 to €50,000, 43% over €50,000).
Refunds are the concrete mechanism for returning overpaid taxes. If a cross-border worker pays more tax in Switzerland than due in Italy (for income declared in both countries), the tax credit in the 730 ensures the refund of the difference. The deadline for submitting the declaration in Italy is by May, allowing an annual verification of the overall tax position.
### AVS, LPP, LAMal: the three pillars of social security and health
Enrollment in AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) is mandatory for any cross-border worker employed in Switzerland. The AVS/AI/IPG contribution rate for the employee is 5.3%, to which AD (unemployment insurance) 1.1% and AC (accident insurance) up to 1.5% depending on the sector are added. The maximum income limit for AD/AC calculation is CHF 148,200 per year.
The LPP (Professional Pension Fund — second pillar) is also mandatory. The employee contribution ranges from 7% to 18% depending on the age group starting from 25 years. This amount is paid directly by the employer to the registered foundation, ensuring a capital accumulation for future pension benefits.
The LAMal (Health Insurance) is not included in the Swiss pay slip: the cross-border worker in the G regime has the option to insure in Switzerland or Italy. If they choose Switzerland, they must subscribe to a private policy with a Ticino (or Swiss) health insurance company, with adult deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, plus a variable monthly premium based on age and canton of residence. If they choose to stay with the Italian system (INPS), they remain subject to Italian contributions but with INPS-SSN coverage.
### Cost of living: where it is cheaper to live
The cost of living in Crodo is significantly lower compared to the main centers of Ticino (Lugano, Locarno, Bellinzona). Rent, food, utilities, and fuel are generally more affordable in Piedmont compared to Swiss cantonal averages. However, it is important to consider commuting costs: fuel, car maintenance, vehicle insurance, and the [vignette](nav:car-cost) (mandatory for driving in Switzerland) reduce the overall cost advantage. For those using public transport (regional trains, cross-border buses), the cost of a cross-border subscription represents a significant item in the monthly budget.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### How to organize: step-by-step towards the transfer
Before moving to Crodo, some administrative steps are essential and must be followed in sequence:
**1. Verify the G permit**: this is the basic requirement for cross-border workers. It must be requested by the Swiss employer in coordination with the cantonal authorities (Migration Section of the Canton Ticino, SECO). The permit is linked to the specific employment contract and requires a formal procedure with the municipality of Crodo and the Italian prefecture.
2. Italian tax registration: once a resident of Crodo, register with the Agenzia delle Entrate of the competent district. Notify the change of residence to the municipality of Crodo to update the registry.
3. Health insurance choice (LAMal): within the registration deadline for the first job in Switzerland, decide whether to opt for Swiss LAMal (with a Ticino health insurance fund) or remain in the Italian INPS system. The choice is not reversible without reasons recognized by the authorities.
4. Open a bank account: not always mandatory, but useful to have an account in Switzerland for receiving the salary without currency commissions. Alternatively, an Italian account with an IBAN compatible with CHF-EUR cross-border transfers works just as well, with attention to the exchange rate.
5. Italian tax declaration (730/Unico): each year, by May, complete the declaration including the gross Swiss income, the withholding tax already paid by Switzerland, and the tax credit in the CE section. This allows the recovery of overpaid amounts and the documentation of residence in Italy for tax purposes.
### Evaluate concrete advantages and disadvantages
Main advantages: lower cost of living than Ticino (about 15–25% savings on rent and consumer goods), tax exemption up to €7,500 annually for old cross-border workers according to the new 2024 agreement, quick access to border crossings (Brogeda, Gaggiolo) with short travel times, a stable Italian community that facilitates social integration and access to Italian services. The Italian-Swiss Convention of December 9, 1976 guarantees normative protection against double taxation.
Real disadvantages: daily commuting (gasoline, car wear, time spent in the car), LAMal costs if the Swiss regime is chosen (about CHF 250–400 monthly depending on age and fund), administrative complexity (double declarations in two countries, tax communications to both states), geographical constraint of the G permit (if you change the Swiss employer, a new permit request is required), limitations of evening entertainment in Crodo compared to the larger urban centers of Ticino.
### Practical tools and next steps
Once moved, keeping track of AVS contributions is essential: the Ticino AVS Compensation Fund keeps an automatic record, but it is good to verify your online statement annually (option available through the SECO and AVS portal). Document all payments to ensure recognition of the contribution career for pension purposes.
To calculate the actual tax impact (gross Swiss salary, AVS/LPP/AD/AC deductions, cantonal and federal withholding tax, reallocation in Italy), use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) of Frontaliere Ticino: enter the annual gross Swiss income, the canton of work (Ticino), your professional category, and the number of cross-border working days, obtaining an estimate of the net in hand and the Italian 730 simulation.
If you have specific questions about permits, procedures, or deductions, contact the competent authorities directly: SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) for G permit and AVS contribution issues, Italian Agenzia delle Entrate for the annual declaration and tax credit. The choice to live in Crodo and work in Ticino is realistically feasible: advanced tax and administrative planning is the key to overall success and savings.

item.title: Living in Varano Borghi, working in Ticino: border guide
item.description: Permit G, taxation and procedure for border workers living in Varano Borghi and working in the Canton of Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - G permit required to work in Ticino as a commuter from Varano Borghi - Double taxation avoided: withholding tax only in Switzerland from 1 Jan 2024 - New commuters: €10,000 annual exemption on employment income - LAMal mandatory; G commuters can opt for Italian insurance
## Key facts - **What**: G permit for EU commuters employed in the Canton of Ticino - When: New Cross-Border Workers Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - Where: Ticino-Italy border (Varano Borghi, province of Varese) - Who: EU/EFTA citizens residing in Italy and employed in Switzerland - Amount: €10,000 annual exemption (new commuters); €7,500 exemption (old commuters, transitional regime 2024–2033)
From 1 January 2024, the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement between Switzerland and Italy, signed on 23 December 2020, has come into force. This agreement introduces a significant change for those, like commuters living in Varano Borghi, who work in the Canton of Ticino. The central aspect is the management of withholding tax: Switzerland applies this tax to the employment income of commuters, but Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the CE section of the 730 declaration. In other words, the tax is withheld only in Switzerland, and in Italy, you receive a credit to offset it.
For new commuters (those who started working in Ticino after 17 July 2023), an annual exemption of €10,000 on employment income is provided. This means that on this portion of earnings, the Swiss withholding tax does not apply. Old commuters—those who were already working in Ticino before 17 July 2023—benefit from a €7,500 exemption in the transitional regime until 2033.
### G permit and withholding tax The G permit is the document that authorizes an EU/EFTA citizen to work in Switzerland as a commuter, i.e., to live in their country of origin (in this case, Italy) and cross the border daily to reach their workplace in the Canton of Ticino. Those living in Varano Borghi and working in Ticino as employees are subject to Swiss withholding tax on employment income. However, from 1 January 2024, the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement has introduced a system that reduces the tax burden. The tax is paid only in Switzerland (withheld at source), and Italy recognizes a tax credit in the 730 declaration to avoid being taxed twice on the same income. The €10,000 exemption for new commuters represents an additional advantage: on this portion of annual income, Switzerland does not apply the withholding tax. Therefore, if your annual employment income in Ticino is €50,000, the first €10,000 is not taxed in Switzerland. The remaining €40,000 is subject to withholding tax according to the applicable federal and cantonal rates. ### Is the G permit convenient? Economic analysis
The decision to move to Varano Borghi to work in Ticino depends on various economic factors. The G permit offers advantages in terms of cost of living—living in border Italy is generally less expensive than residing in Ticino—but it also has costs that need to be carefully evaluated.
As a cross-border worker, you are subject to Swiss AVS/AI/IPG contributions (5.3% of your salary as an employee) and other pension contributions. Health insurance coverage (LAMal) is mandatory in Switzerland; however, as a G cross-border worker, you have the option: you can remain insured with your Italian insurance or opt for Swiss LAMal. Find out how it works for cross-border workers and what your options are.
In Italy, you must also pay INPS contributions to your Italian employer (if you work part-time in Italy) or you are covered by Swiss contributions if you work exclusively in Ticino. The Convention between Italy and Switzerland of December 9, 1976 coordinates pension schemes to avoid contribution gaps.
### Tax refunds and savings opportunities
The most interesting aspect of the €10,000 allowance is the gross savings on taxes. If your employer in Ticino withholds less withholding tax on this portion, the net amount you receive monthly is higher compared to cross-border workers without an allowance. In the transitional regime (until 2033), cross-border workers who were already working in Ticino before July 17, 2023 enjoy an exemption of €7,500, while new cross-border workers receive €10,000. Additionally, the Italian 730 declaration allows you to [request refunds](nav:ristorni) if Swiss withholdings exceed Italian taxes due. For example, if the Swiss withholding tax is higher than the corresponding Italian tax, the balance is refunded. This mechanism is possible thanks to the Italo-Swiss Convention, which recognizes the tax credit in the Italian system.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Checklist: how to become a cross-border worker in Ticino
If you decide to move to Varano Borghi and work in the Canton Ticino as a cross-border worker G, here are the main steps.
Step 1: Ensure you have a job offer. The G permit is granted on a contractual basis: your employer must offer an employee role, and you must have a written proposal before applying for the permit.
Step 2: Apply for the G permit at the Sportello Migrazione (SEM) of the Canton Ticino or at the competent office of your municipality of residence in Italy (in Lombardy, it is usually the Migrazione Service of the province of Varese). The application form asks for personal information, employer data, and the proposed salary.
Step 3: Register your address in Varano Borghi. You must have an actual residence in Italy. This implies a rental contract or ownership, and a registration with the municipality of Varano Borghi.
Step 4: Register with INPS as a cross-border worker. In Italy, communicate your status as a cross-border worker to INPS. Even if you work exclusively in Switzerland, you must be registered in the INPS system to coordinate the contribution periods.
Step 5: Choose your health insurance. Within 30 days of starting work, choose whether to keep your Italian LAMal or subscribe to a Swiss LAMal. Communicate your choice to your employer.
Step 6: Prepare the Italian 730 declaration. Every year, even if the withholding tax is already deducted in Switzerland, you must submit the 730 in Italy by April 30 (deadline, unless extended) to request the tax credit and any refunds. Before moving, [use our calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate your net income considering Swiss tax rates, AVS/LPP contributions, Italian taxes, and daily commuting costs (A2/A9 highway, parking in Ticino, gasoline). Also consider the cost of living: rent, utilities, insurance, and groceries in Varano Borghi are generally cheaper than in Ticino, but daily commuting has a significant fixed cost that must be included in your calculations.

item.title: Living in Besnate and working in Ticino: as a border worker
item.description: How taxation, rights and practical organisation work for those who live in Besnate and work in Ticino as border workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Withholding tax only in Switzerland for cross-border workers - New Cross-Border Workers Agreement effective from 1 January 2024 - EUR 10,000 threshold for new cross-border workers - Permit G mandatory for the Ticino-Italy border
## Key facts - **What**: Living in Lombardy and working in the Canton of Ticino as a cross-border worker - When: Regulation in effect from 1 January 2024 - Where: Northern Ticino-Italy border (crossings: Brogeda, Chiasso) - Who: Workers residing in Italy who work in Switzerland - Permit: Cross-border worker permit G (required before employment) - Taxation: Withholding tax in Switzerland; Italian tax credit - Threshold: EUR 10,000 annually for new cross-border workers (from 17 July 2023) - Legal basis: New Agreement signed on 23 December 2020, Italian Law 83/2023
Living in Besnate, province of Varese, and working in the Canton of Ticino is a choice that thousands of cross-border workers make daily. The decision to move across the border involves practical considerations - travel time, cost of living, housing - and tax considerations, with Swiss withholding tax and social security contributions (AVS and LPP). The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, which came into effect on 1 January 2024, introduced significant changes: new cross-border workers benefit from a EUR 10,000 annual threshold, while those who were already cross-border workers before 17 July 2023 fall under a transitional regime with a EUR 7,500 threshold until 2033. Italy, through the tax credit in the model 730, prevents double taxation.
### The context of the Besnate-Ticino cross-border worker
Those who choose to live in Besnate while working in Ticino fall into the category of cross-border workers who cross the Italian-Swiss border daily. The Canton of Ticino, with a strong economic structure in sectors such as healthcare, finance, tourism, and industry, attracts numerous workers from the province of Varese and neighboring areas of Lombardy. Cross-border workers pay [AVS and LPP contributions](nav:pension) directly from their Swiss paycheck - a well-established practice thanks to the Convention against Double Taxation signed on 9 December 1976 between Italy and Switzerland.
The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement, signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, came into effect on 1 January 2024. This reform changed the taxation criteria, introducing different regimes: those who were already cross-border workers before 17 July 2023 benefit from a transitional regime with a EUR 7,500 annual threshold until 2033, while new cross-border workers have access to a EUR 10,000 threshold. A crucial aspect remains unchanged: the Swiss withholding tax is the only tax withheld. Italy applies the tax credit in the CE section of the income tax return (model 730) to avoid double taxation. ### The payslip and contributions
From the Swiss payslip, social security and insurance contributions are automatically deducted. The AVS/AI/IPG rate is 5.3% for the employee, while unemployment insurance (AD/AC) represents 1.1% of the gross salary (capped at CHF 148,200). Accident insurance (LAINF) varies between 0.7% and 1.5%, while the pension fund (LPP) amounts to a percentage ranging from 7% to 18% depending on the worker's age bracket (from 25 years onwards).
A commuter from Besnate working in Ticino is entitled to receive periodic extracts of their contribution position through the SECO system. These payments ensure Swiss pension coverage and protection against workplace accidents, rights that accumulate with the Italian position at INPS (coordinated by the 1976 Convention).
### Health insurance (LAMal) and options
Category G commuters have the option to choose Swiss LAMal. The deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500 annually, depending on the chosen policy and coverage model. Many commuters choose to keep Italian health insurance (CMI) for continuity of care, a decision that should be carefully evaluated in terms of premiums, coverage, and access to Ticino healthcare facilities. [Discover LAMal and CMI options](nav:health) Choosing LAMal allows the commuter to access Swiss healthcare facilities directly (EOC hospitals in Ticino, cantonal polyclinics), while maintaining Italian CMI requires checks for reciprocity.
### Tax scenarios and declarations
A new commuter (after July 17, 2023) living in Besnate and earning CHF 60,000 annually gross in Ticino applies a EUR 10,000 exemption on the Italian taxable base. The Swiss withholding tax is calculated based on the rate in effect in the canton and municipality of work. The Italian tax credit in the 730 form ensures that they do not pay taxes on both sides. Older commuters (before July 17, 2023) benefit from an annual EUR 7,500 exemption until 2033, allowing them a gradual transition to the new regime. [Simulate your net salary with the calculator](nav:calculator).
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Checklist: before moving to Besnate to work in Ticino
Before completing the move, make sure you have all the elements in order:
**Essential documentation**: G permit for cross-border workers (required before starting employment), employment contract signed by the employer in Ticino, Italian tax code, valid ID card, and a Swiss bank account (optional but recommended for receiving the paycheck).
Declarations and registrations: Notify the Italian Tax Agency of the move and proceed with the change of address at the Italian municipality. Register with INPS as an employee working abroad, providing the data of the employer in Ticino. Inform your Swiss employer of all Italian banking and tax details.
Insurance: Consider switching to Swiss LAMal or keeping Italian CMI. Ensure that accident insurance coverage for the commute to work is active (usually covered by Swiss LAINF if the accident occurs during working hours).
Taxes and refunds: Schedule a consultation with a tax advisor specializing in cross-border workers to open an annual file. Check your eligibility for CVA (Advance Payment Credits) refunds based on your contribution situation.
### The first months: what to expect
After the move, your first Swiss paycheck will arrive with the necessary deductions (AVS, LPP, LAINF, and withholding taxes). By June 30 of the following year, you will submit the Italian tax return to the CAF or through a tax advisor, indicating the income earned in Ticino and applying the cross-border exemption. Meanwhile, maintain regular communication with INPS for updates on your foreign contribution status.
### Tools and resources for cross-border workers
Use [the salary calculator](nav:calculator) to simulate the tax impact of your Swiss paycheck considering the applicable cross-border exemption (EUR 7,500 or EUR 10,000 depending on the registration date). [Compare the cost of living](nav:cost-of-living) between Besnate and neighboring Ticino areas to assess whether this choice offers the best balance between housing costs, services, and proximity to work.
### Key deadlines for cross-border workers
Every cross-border worker must submit the Italian tax return by June 30 of the following year (for the 730 model through CAF or tax advisor). Notification to the SEM (Swiss State Secretariat for Migration) of changes in address or residence must be made within 14 days of the change. Renewal of the G permit: every 5 years, provided the employment relationship in Ticino continues.
